change: Live JPEG files and temporary writes now include the task fencing token; API only reads the running task's current fencing generation. Old Worker teardown cannot remove the newer lease's frame.

release.build_method: Offline Docker overlays on the 66 host using the pre-existing verified API/Worker runtime images as pinned local bases, updated source files from the 94f297b git archive, and TypeScript compilation within each image. This is not a fresh lockfile/full dependency installation.
release.standard_build_blocker: The full worker Dockerfile build could not fetch npm dependencies: registry.npmjs.org timed out on 66; the blocking build job was explicitly stopped.

isolated_chromium_tests.T51_live_capture: passed; 7 distinct hashes from 7 sampled frames; cleanup verified
isolated_chromium_tests.T54_stale_vs_new_fence: passed; old Worker stop does not remove newer live file

isolated_chromium_concurrency.resource_limits: network none, 3 CPUs, 3 GB memory, PID cap 512, 256 MB /dev/shm

limitations: The T50 load is 108 Chromium sessions over 23.6 seconds, not 8 hours or a full live orchestrator/model end-to-end soak.
The API behavior was checked for anonymous access and health, not a live authorized HTTP frame delivery during a new business run.
Current anonymity/non-submitting restrictions and imperfect pixel-redaction coverage remain unchanged.
A hard-killed Worker can leave an expired fence-specific file until a separate bounded garbage-collection policy removes it; expiry and the current-fence API binding prevent serving it.
Full reproducible Docker builds are still blocked by npm registry connectivity from the 66 host; the offline overlays are test-environment deployment images, not production release qualification.
Other documented P0 gaps, including failure-injection recovery under concurrent orchestration and broad LLM semantic repair accuracy, remain open.
